title: Correct final displacement
description: Essential: The student's final numerical answer for the total vertical displacement must be 60.0 m.

title: Newton's Law application
description: Important: The student must correctly apply Newton's second law (F_net = ma) to relate the normal force from the graph to the elevator's acceleration in each time segment.

title: Kinematic segmentation
description: Important: The solution must correctly divide the motion into three distinct phases (0-2 s, 2-6 s, 6-8 s) based on the force graph and calculate displacement for each.

title: Velocity continuity
description: Important: The student must correctly use the final velocity from one phase as the initial velocity for the next phase (e.g., v at t=2s is used for phases 2 and 3).

title: Correct kinematic equations
description: Important: The student must apply the correct equations of motion (e.g., x = 1/2 at², x = vt, v = u + at) for uniformly accelerated and constant velocity segments.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: All calculations should maintain consistent units (kg, m, s, N) leading to displacement in meters.

title: Sign error in acceleration
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly assigns the sign to the acceleration in the 6-8 second segment (deceleration upwards should be negative if up is positive).

title: Misinterpreting force graph
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student confuses the body's pressure on the floor (given) with the normal force on the body, or fails to subtract weight to find net force.
